title: Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines for LLMs suffer from high latency in the retrieval phase due to expensive nearest-neighbor search over large knowledge bases, and existing profiling of the interplay between retrieval accuracy and generation phase cost is lacking. The choice between exact and approximate retrieval is not well characterized in terms of end-to-end latency vs. accuracy.
method: The paper profiles several RAG execution pipelines to characterize the complex interplay between retrieval and generation phases. It demonstrates that exact nearest-neighbor search, though more expensive in isolation, can outperform approximate retrieval end-to-end because an exact retrieval model selects a smaller, higher-precision set of documents, reducing the inference burden on the autoregressive generation stage. Based on this, the paper motivates and proposes hardware/system acceleration of exact nearest-neighbor search for RAG, using optimized data structures and computation strategies (specific details not available from abstract).

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper lsCOMP: Efficient Light Source Compression
problem: Reproducibility report meta-paper: evaluation of artifact reproducibility for lsCOMP paper (full paper analysis not available from abstract)
method: Artifact evaluation conducted by SC25 Reproducibility Committee member, assessing the Artifact Description and Evaluation appendix of the lsCOMP paper.

title: Automatic Generation of Mappings for Distributed Fourier Operations
problem: Distributed Fourier transform libraries provide rigid implementations forcing developers to mold code around FFT computations, missing opportunities to minimize communication between Fourier operations and surrounding numerical computations.
method: Automatic mapping generation for multi-dimensional distributed Fourier operations using novel non-linear iterative formulation. Leverages Z3 SMT solver to optimize across both Fourier and linear algebra operations, minimizing communication steps across key MPI collectives while selecting optimal grid shape.

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Supercritical Flame Simulation at Detailed Chemistry and Real-Fluid Accuracy Towards Trillion-Cell Scale
problem: Supercritical flame simulations with detailed chemistry and real-fluid transport have been limited to millions of cells due to computational cost.
method: DeepFlame: neural-network-enabled simulator with optimizations in parallel computing, efficiency, and I/O; tuned for Sunway and Fugaku.

title: Saving Energy with Per-Variable Bitwidth Speculation
problem: Compilers for tiny embedded devices directly translate source-level variable bitwidths (e.g., 32-bit integers) to binary without exploiting the fact that most variables use far fewer bits than declared at runtime. This wastes energy in computations and memory traffic on highly optimized, energy-constrained devices where further traditional optimizations are difficult.
method: BitSpec is a compiler-architecture co-design: the compiler statically narrows variable bitwidths to their predicted (expected) needs and emits speculative narrow-bitwidth instructions. The hardware monitors live values in speculative variables; when a value overflows the narrowed representation, hardware reports a misspeculation event to software, which re-executes the affected computation at the original (safe) bitwidth. This speculation-recovery loop ensures correctness while capturing energy savings during the common case where narrow widths suffice.

title: SmaRTLy: RTL Optimization with Logic Inferencing and Structural Rebuilding
problem: Traditional RTL multiplexer optimization in tools like Yosys only monitors control port values during tree traversal, missing intrinsic logical relationships among signals and opportunities for structural optimization.
method: Develops logic inferencing techniques to identify and remove redundant multiplexer trees, then restructures remaining multiplexers by exploiting intrinsic logical relationships among signals to reduce overall gate count in the design.

title: Assessing Page Reclamation Mechanisms for Linux
problem: Understanding and quantifying the performance characteristics of Linux page reclamation policies remains challenging. Need for comprehensive analysis of decision-making overhead and reclamation effectiveness.
method: Lightweight profiler to measure decision overhead and reclamation effectiveness of Linux's Two-Queue LRU (2QLRU) and Multi-Generational LRU (MGLRU) policies. Evaluation across seven diverse applications under various memory constraints.

title: eDKM: An Efficient and Accurate Train-Time Weight Clustering for Large Language Models
problem: Differentiable KMeans (DKM) weight clustering achieves state-of-the-art compression accuracy for LLMs but its memory complexity makes train-time application to billion-parameter LLMs nearly impossible, requiring far more GPU memory than available on any single device.
method: eDKM reduces DKM memory footprint during the backward pass by: (1) uniquification — detecting and deduplicating identical tensors before CPU offload to avoid redundant copies; (2) sharding — splitting large tensors across memory partitions for further compression. Both techniques apply to the intermediate tensors that must be retained on CPU during DKM's backward pass. This reduces the train-time memory footprint of a decoder layer by 130x, enabling fine-tuning and compression of a 7B LLaMA model to 3b/weight on standard GPU hardware.

title: 15.5 Event-Based Spatially Zooming Neural Interface IC with 10nW/Input Reconfigurable-Inverter Fabric and Input-Adaptive Quantization
problem: Large-scale neural interface ICs require million+ electrodes for brain interfaces, but face two bottlenecks: neural ADC power dissipation (>50× higher than 10nW/input target) and output data rate (200Gb/s required for 1M electrodes at 8b/25kHz).
method: Event-driven neural interface using spatially-selective zooming (exploiting neural spiking sparsity without information loss), 10nW/input reconfigurable-inverter ADC fabric, and input-adaptive quantization that reduces data rate by selecting only informative electrodes and adapting bit-width per channel.

title: Up and Running with Rapidus : How Japan and Cutting-Edge Technologies are Transforming Semiconductor Manufacturing
problem: Japan's semiconductor manufacturing capacity has declined; existing fabs use older process technologies limiting competitiveness in advanced node production.
method: Rapidus (Japanese government-backed fab) deploys cutting-edge manufacturing technologies including EUV lithography, advanced packaging, and vertical integration strategies. The presentation discusses process node scaling, yield optimization, and ramp strategies.

title: BLAZE: Exploiting Hybrid Parallelism and Size-customized Kernels to Accelerate BLASTP on GPUs
problem: BLASTP (sequence alignment) on GPUs remains slower than optimized CPU/multithreaded implementations despite GPU acceleration attempts.
method: BLAZE combines hybrid fine/coarse-grained parallelism, sequence-length-customized kernels, and GPU-specific optimizations for BLASTP.

title: ChameleonEC: Exploiting Tunability of Erasure Coding for Low-Interference Repair
problem: Erasure coding repair traffic in distributed storage systems contends with foreground I/O traffic over shared network bandwidth, slowing repair progress and degrading service quality. Existing repair mechanisms lack dynamic adaptability to varying foreground traffic patterns and unexpected slow nodes (stragglers).
method: ChameleonEC decomposes repair plans into fine-grained repair tasks and uses three mechanisms: (1) repair task assignment that saturates unoccupied bandwidth while avoiding contention with foreground traffic; (2) repair path establishment that orchestrates elastic transmission routings across dispatched tasks; (3) straggler-aware re-scheduling that dynamically retunes task transmissions and repair plans to bypass slow nodes. The system is implemented and evaluated on Amazon EC2.

title: Variable Read Disturbance: An Experimental Analysis of Temporal Variation in DRAM Read Disturbance
problem: DRAM read disturbance (RowHammer/RowPress) mitigation techniques rely on accurate per-row read disturbance threshold (RDT) characterization, but the RDT of individual DRAM rows is not static: it varies significantly and unpredictably over time, making accurate characterization with a limited number of measurements infeasible.
method: Experimental characterization of 160 DDR4 chips and 4 HBM2 chips from three major manufacturers using repeated RDT measurements on the same rows over time. The study observes that the minimum RDT of a row only appears after up to 94,467 repeated measurements, with the minimum being 3.5x smaller than the observed maximum. Analysis covers the effects of chip density, technology node, data pattern, aggressor row open time, and temperature on RDT variability. Guardbanding and ECC (SECDED/Chipkill) approaches are evaluated as mitigations.

title: CORD: Low-Latency, Bandwidth-Efficient and Scalable Release Consistency via Directory Ordering
problem: In multi-processing-unit systems (CPU-GPU, multi-GPU) using write-through cache coherence with release consistency, the source processor must serialize write ordering through itself to the LLC directory, generating unnecessary round-trip communication that increases latency, interconnect traffic, and energy for producer-consumer AI/ML workloads.
method: CORD is a cache coherence protocol that relocates write-through ordering responsibility from the source processor to the LLC directory. The directory accumulates write-through operations and enforces release consistency locally, eliminating source-to-directory round-trips. Novel metadata compression mechanisms minimize the storage overhead of tracking in-flight ordered writes at the directory, and the protocol is designed to scale across multiple directories without serialization bottlenecks. Evaluation is performed on gem5.

title: 32.6 A Dynamic-RON-Diminished Bidirectional GaN Load Switch with Inrush Current Protection and Spike Attenuation
problem: Bidirectional GaN load switches for 48V EV power systems require both reverse-current blocking and bidirectional current transfer; monolithic bidirectional GaN (Bi-GaN) devices reduce on-resistance vs. discrete back-to-back solutions but suffer from overstress during turn-off when gate-to-source voltage exceeds breakdown limits, requiring complex turn-off selectors.
method: A dynamic-RON-diminished bidirectional GaN load switch using a monolithic bidirectional GaN device with CD (common-drain) topology. The design employs a novel turn-off control strategy that dynamically selects between gate-to-first-terminal or gate-to-second-terminal paths to avoid overstress, combined with inrush-current protection and spike-attenuation circuits.

title: FedEDA: Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning in EDA
problem: EDA ML models require large circuit benchmarks for training, but intellectual property security concerns prevent companies from sharing raw circuit data, creating data scarcity that limits progress in ML-driven EDA.
method: FedEDA is a federated learning aggregation algorithm designed for EDA, enabling participants to exchange model weights instead of sharing raw circuit data. The algorithm leverages Rent's Rule and circuit size to capture hierarchical structure, mitigating data imbalance issues among participants and improving weight aggregation quality.
